limits: Python and libraries on this page: the examples that run do so in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with Pyodide's Pillow 11.3.0 and NumPy 2.2.5 and the pytesseract 0.3.13 wheel this page carries, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with pytesseract 0.3.13, Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4, OpenCV 5.0.0.93, PyAutoGUI 0.9.54 and the real Tesseract (the apt 5.3.4, and 5.5.3 and 4.1.1 built from source), NAPS2 8.5.1 and OCRmyPDF 17.13.0. Each example that runs was compared with its recorded result by value.

Recorded, not run: 66 examples need the Tesseract program, another program (NAPS2, OCRmyPDF, apt, Python itself), the language data files of the machine, a font file, the zip of the book's online materials, or print what Python 3.14 or Pillow 12 print and the browser's older ones do not; a browser's Python cannot start a program or download that zip. Pictures: 7 recorded pictures drawn by the research programs (under ColumnLayout, Deskew, IsoCodes, NapsInputLanguage, SmallText, TimeoutArgument, Upscaling) are shown beside their examples, labelled 'Recorded picture, not made on this page'; they are SHA-256 checked when the page is made, and none is made from a picture of the book.

The screen-reading program ran in the recording on a virtual X display (Xvfb) with ImageMagick's display and PyAutoGUI, a local stand-in for a screen; nobody saw the picture and no real screen or browser was read. Nothing ran on Windows or macOS and no scanner was used.

The page embeds one wheel, pytesseract 0.3.13 (Apache License 2.0, SHA-256 checked), and no file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes holding 91 files; ocr-example.png, frankenstein.png and frankenstein_jpn.png are among them). The licence of the zip and of its pictures is an open question for the owner; pictures made from them are not on this page (03-materials/ch22/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md).

NOT EXECUTED: Windows and macOS (the installers, Homebrew, the PATH of Windows); the Flatpak of NAPS2; a flatbed scanner; the large language model step; a real screen with a real browser; the UB Mannheim installer page (it answered 403 through the proxy); the commit the course pins; the final Python 3.15 (uv offered 3.15.0b4); pytesseract 0.3.4, 0.3.7 and 0.3.8 (no wheels; 0.3.12 does not exist); the text of the PDF embedded in Figure 22-2; and a photograph (the single request to Wikimedia Commons answered 429).

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-13 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 40,521 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology) and the book's other pages and links. The book pins pytesseract==0.3.10 in Appendix A, which imports pkgutil.find_loader, a function Python 3.14 removed; PyPI lists no 0.3.11 or 0.3.12.

One program was run under 11 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.14, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6, 3.15.0b4): 0 of 19 items differ between them. Small programs were also run under 14 Pillow releases (0 of 9 items differ) and pytesseract releases on three interpreters (21 runs; 2 of 10 items differ, for example the type of the confidences image_to_data returns); see interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json. The 16 items of the third-party record were run with the newest releases and with the book's pins.
